title: Reading Regression Tests Without Fooling Yourself
utility_use_case: A reliability engineer investigating an intermittent service slowdown can run the utility on an application log to get a quick count of severity labels and lines matching terms such as `timeout`. The JSON can feed a dashboard or an incident notebook without embedding message text, which helps avoid moving sensitive details into summary artifacts. Counts help prioritize follow-up, but they do not identify root cause, unique incidents, or statistical significance. In a research workflow, the same aggregates can be recorded alongside experimental conditions for descriptive monitoring. The regression topic motivates disciplined interpretation of measurements: like coefficient tests, log counts are evidence with a scope and assumptions, not an automatic explanation of a system. The book section does not specify this utility; it is an engineering companion for collecting compact observability summaries.
